title: What Happens When Gliese 710 Passes Through the Oort Cloud?
description:
What Happens When a Star Passes Through Our Solar System?
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F-jImX5h7ws

Sunlight reaches Earth in about eight minutes, yet it would take months to travel out to the distant Oort Cloud where the orange dwarf Gliese 710 is heading. When the star passes through in about 1.3 million years, its gravity will brush through that vast cloud of icy bodies and nudge the comets nearest its path.

Sources: Bailer-Jones (2022), The Astrophysical Journal Letters 935 L9 — Gaia DR3 encounter distance and timing (https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/ac816a) · Berski & Dybczyński (2016), Astronomy & Astrophysics 595 L10 — Gliese 710 trajectory through the Oort Cloud and comet perturbation (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201629835) · NASA Science, Oort Cloud Facts — the distant comet reservoir (https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/oort-cloud/facts/).

Pictures: NASA GSFC Solar Dynamics Observatory solar-flare eruption video, ESA/Gaia/DPAC proper-motion starfield animation (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO), NASA photograph of Comet NEOWISE over Washington, D.C. by Bill Ingalls, ESO La Silla New Technology Telescope night-sky time-lapse (CC BY 4.0), and NASA STS-83 Space Shuttle photograph of Comet Hale-Bopp, alongside original animated explainers and AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: NASA/SDO; ESA/Gaia/DPAC (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/igo/); NASA/Bill Ingalls; ESO (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); NASA/JSC.
